newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine researches first foreign bond issue-FinMin.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine researches first foreign bond issue-FinMin.

text.p: Ukraine is researching numerous markets to host its first foreign bond sometime this year, the deputy finance minister said on Thursday.

"We are researching. There are many markets, not just the Euro but the Samurai, Yankee, the chocolate -- or Swiss -- market, and Bulldog bonds," Mykhailo Honcharuk said at a news conference. "But we have made no final decision."
Honcharuk said Ukraine was also deciding on which company to hire to conduct its rating.
"A rating would allow Ukraine to enter markets to get money, but not only through markets," he said. "If a country gets a rating it increases investor confidence."
He added that it would also enable cities to issue municipal bonds.
Last year the government announced it planned to issue $250 million of foreign bonds by the end of the first quarter of 1997 and that it was reviewing a list of companies to act as agents.
